Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant today is taken on record.
Vide order dated 08.08.2024, the applicant was released on interim bail.

The order dated 08.08.2024 is quotes below:-
Heard Sri Sudhakar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Mohd. Jaid,
learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of applicants in Case Crime No.117 of 2022,
under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504 of IPC, Police Station Kadadham, District Kaushambi Indrajeet Singh vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155601985/
1 with the prayer to enlarge the applicants on bail.
4.

entities.text: Kaushambi Indrajeet Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present matter.
The applicant is ready to pay the entire amount of Rs.7 lakh within three months through RTGS or Demand Draft, if he is released on interim bail.
It is further submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 23.08.2022 and that in case he is released on interim bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant have no objection if the applicant pay the entire amount due upon him.

6. In view of the statement made by learned counsel for the applicant, let applicant- Indrajeet Singh,
involved in the aforesaid case crime be released on interim bail for a period of three months from the date of his release on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
(1). The applicant will not tamper with the prosecution evidence during the trial.
(2). The applicant will not influence any witness.
(3).
The applicant will appear before the trial Court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(4). The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
7. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move an application before this Court seeking cancellation of the bail.
8. The applicant shall surrender before the court concerned immediately after three months from the date of his release.
The concerned court shall submit a report to this court about the surrender of the applicant.
9. The applicant shall return the amount of Rs.7 lakh in the account of the informant through Demand Draft or RTGS within three months from the date of his release.
10. List on 12.11.2024 for final hearing of bail application.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has deposited Rs. 7 Lac before the Trial Court through Demand Draft No. 45180300002600000005116 dated 04.11.2024 and the same has been received by the first informant on 05.11.2024, as such the applicant has complied with the terms and conditions imposed by this Court vide order dated 08.08.2024.

Learned counsel for the Indrajeet Singh vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155601985/
2 applicant prays that the applicant may be granted regular bail.
